records.summary_text:
Hungary is in a fast-improving post-Orbán transition. The most acute traveler-facing risk — the 2025 Pride ban with facial-recognition identification of attendees — has stopped: the 2026 Budapest Pride was held freely after the April 2026 election in which Péter Magyar's Tisza party won a supermajority, ending 16 years of previous rule.

records.name: Greece
records.summary_text:
Greece is a workable destination with a clear law-versus-practice gap. The legal framework is among Europe's strongest — it ranks 7th on the ILGA-Europe Rainbow Map, has banned conversion therapy and intersex infant surgery, has a hate-crime law covering gender identity, and legalised same-sex marriage in 2024 (the first Orthodox-majority country to do so). There are no trans-specific border or bathroom restrictions, and the government is progressive with an improving trajectory.

But the social reality lags the law. A mob of about 150 people assaulted two trans people in Thessaloniki;

records.name: Czechia
records.summary_text:
Czechia is broadly workable with an improving trajectory and a major welcoming tourist hub (Prague), offset by unprepared detention systems and elevated baseline social hostility. If detained, the system is unprepared: a documented case shows police mishandling the extradition-detention of an HIV-positive trans foreigner; safeguards ordered at the highest court level exist, but practice is inconsistent.
